solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Man from another planet intercepted by copper

indicators.note: a planet intercepted by copper has the metal's symbol cut into the middle of it

parts.note: Mars is a planet other than our own
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A visiting alien is stopped in its tracks by a police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man from another planet' reads as one phrase for an alien; 'Man' alone is the definition and the planet is the wordplay. 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is the element.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcus is a male first name, so a man may be called by it.

clue.text: Mountain features exist, appearing above ascending group

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece appears above the second

parts.note: are means exist

indicators.note: in a down entry ascending means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a set is a group

explanation.surface: Mountain ridges exist above a climbing party.
explanation.definitionFit: Aretes are sharp mountain ridges carved by glaciers.

clue.text: Friendship of dear America going awry

indicators.note: going awry means going wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Friendship with dear America is turning sour.
explanation.definitionFit: Camaraderie is the comradely trust and goodwill between friends.

clue.text: Oddly saying academic work offers reconciliation of ideas?

indicators.note: oddly takes the odd-numbered letters of the word

parts.note: a thesis is an academic dissertation

explanation.surface: A strange remark suggests that an academic paper reconciles ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: Synthesis is the combining of separate ideas into one whole.

clue.text: Worthless plane makers suffering setback — evidence of metal fatigue?

indicators.note: a setback sends the makers' name backwards, so it is read in reverse

parts.note: MiG is the Russian aircraft design bureau that builds fighter planes
metal that has fatigued shows a crack

explanation.surface: An aircraft manufacturer is in trouble after its planes show stress fractures.
explanation.walkthrough: MiG, the Russian aircraft bureau, read backwards gives GIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Gimcrack describes showy but flimsy, shoddy goods of little value.

clue.text: Miss one constellation as astronomer with primitive telescope

parts.note: a miss is a girl or gal
I is the Roman numeral for one
Leo is the constellation of the lion

explanation.surface: An early stargazer with a crude instrument fails to see a constellation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' reads as a verb, fail to see, but it is the noun for a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Galileo built early refracting telescopes and used them to study the heavens.

clue.text: Notes a particular male going the wrong way

indicators.note: going the wrong way means going backwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: some can mean a particular, as in some man

explanation.surface: Notes record a certain man heading in the wrong direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Memos are short written notes or messages.

clue.text: Difficulty chipping end off stone

indicators.note: the last letter is chipped away from the gem's name

parts.note: a ruby is a precious stone

explanation.surface: A jeweller struggles to chip a corner off a gem.
explanation.definitionFit: A rub is a snag or obstacle, as in Hamlet's 'there's the rub'.

clue.text: Underground workers using dogs to catch snooper finally

indicators.note: the dogs catch the letter, holding it inside them

parts.note: collies are sheepdogs

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Miners use dogs to track down a spy.
explanation.definitionFit: Colliers are coal miners, who work below ground.

clue.text: Time of revolution finishing — grand for short time

indicators.note: grand is put in place of short time, the usual sense of one thing standing for another

parts.note: terminal means final or finishing
T is the abbreviation for time
G is slang shorthand for a grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A period of upheaval is ending, and something big replaces a brief moment.
explanation.walkthrough: Germinal was the seventh month of the French Revolutionary calendar, so 'revolution' means the French Revolution, not a turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Germinal was a spring month in the calendar adopted during the French Revolution.

clue.text: Phone city in Alabama

definitions.meaning: a cell phone is called by this portable-sounding name in Britain
a port city on the Gulf coast of Alabama

explanation.surface: Someone is told to ring a city in the American South.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a portable phone, and the Alabama port city of that name.

clue.text: Hard world where things can get very hot

definitions.text: where things can get very hot

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
the earth is our world

explanation.surface: A harsh planet where temperatures soar.
explanation.definitionFit: A fireplace floor is where a fire burns, so it gets very hot there.

clue.text: Threat to health, minute one found in time

parts.note: to minute something is to record or list it

indicators.note: one is found within the time, so it sits inside it

parts.note: an era is a period of time
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A health hazard is spotted in tiny form just in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minute' looks like the adjective 'tiny', but it is the verb meaning to record, giving LIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Listeria is a bacterium causing food poisoning, a danger to health.

clue.text: Industrial German city — it upset colleague, by its very nature

parts.note: Essen is an industrial city in the Ruhr

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: an ally is an associate or colleague

explanation.surface: In a German factory city, something has upset a co-worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Essentially means in essence, fundamentally, by nature.

clue.text: Unease of party politician with nothing certain

parts.note: a disco is a dance party
MP is a Member of Parliament
O looks like zero, nothing
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A politician at a party feels uneasy despite seeming sure of nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Discomposure is a state of agitation or disturbed calm, which is unease.

clue.text: Journalists meeting knotty situation to the north kept going

parts.note: the press means journalists

indicators.note: in a down entry going north means upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a node is a knot or point of complication

explanation.surface: Reporters face a tricky problem up north.
explanation.definitionFit: To press on is to continue resolutely, carrying on regardless.

clue.text: Type of information encountered — notice a brief acknowledgement

parts.note: met means encountered
an ad is a notice or advertisement
ta is a short informal thank you

explanation.surface: Someone finds a notice and gives a quick thanks for the information.
explanation.definitionFit: Metadata is data describing other data, a kind of information.

clue.text: One rogue's run off — "brainy" operator?

indicators.note: off here means gone wrong or awry, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A villain makes a getaway, leaving a clever surgeon behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off' reads as running away; it signals the anagram of ONE ROGUES RUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A brain surgeon operates on the brain, so in a punning sense this operator is brainy.

clue.text: A bitter uprising separating two sides on the left?

indicators.note: the inner letters go between the two sides, separating them

parts.note: R and L stand for right and left, the two sides

indicators.note: in a down entry an uprising reads upwards, so backwards

parts.note: acid means sharp or bitter

explanation.surface: A bitter revolt splits two political sides.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that radicals are not always on the left.
explanation.definitionFit: Radical politics is often associated with the left wing, wanting sweeping change.

clue.text: Was monarch no good to be restricted?

indicators.note: no means without, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: a monarch who ruled reigned

explanation.surface: A king asks whether his bad rule should be curbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Reined means held back or curbed, as a horse is by its reins.

clue.text: Lifelong publishing employee made fast progress

parts.note: a career is a lifelong profession
ED is short for editor, who works in publishing

explanation.surface: A long-serving editor rose rapidly through the ranks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lifelong' is used as a noun-like adjective for career, one's life's work.
explanation.definitionFit: To career is to rush along at speed, so the past tense means sped onward.

clue.text: Dish on Japanese menu? Head of restaurant has the final word

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the word

parts.note: amen is said at the end of a prayer, the last word

explanation.surface: In a Japanese eatery, the head waiter has the last say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of restaurant' looks like a person; it picks R.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramen is a Japanese noodle soup dish.

clue.text: Youngster, said by Australian to be a chip off the old block?

definitions.text: a chip off the old block?

indicators.note: the Australian accent turns the vowel of the youngster's word toward an i sound

parts.note: a young shaver is a youngster

explanation.surface: An Australian calls a child a chip off the old block.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shaver' is old slang for a lad; in a stereotyped Australian accent it comes out with a short i.
explanation.definitionFit: A shiver is a splinter or fragment, so a chip broken off a block of wood is one.

clue.text: Month seeing end of winter has sheep getting grass

parts.note: March is the month that sees winter end, abbreviated Mar
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: As winter ends one month, a sheep is out grazing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End of winter' looks like a call for its last letter, but the whole phrase describes March, shortened to MAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Marram is a coarse grass that binds sand dunes.

clue.text: Charity event in tabloid?

definitions.meaning: a British student carnival held to raise funds for charity
a disparaging word for a low-quality newspaper

explanation.surface: A charity event is written up in a tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a British student charity carnival, and a disparaging word for a newspaper.

clue.text: Cooking two fish to cover starter for dinner

indicators.note: the two fish cover the starter, so it goes between them

parts.note: cod and ling are both sea fish, written together

indicators.note: starter for dinner means its opening letter

explanation.surface: A meal of two kinds of fish is being prepared before the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' looks like a first course but just picks the D of dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: To coddle is to cook eggs gently in water below boiling, so coddling is a way of cooking.

clue.text: Alarming changes on the border

indicators.note: the word undergoes changes, its letters being reordered

explanation.surface: Worrying alterations are happening along a frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: Marginal means at the edge or margin, so lying on a border.

clue.text: Revolutionary period involved in no end of vile execution by drowning

indicators.note: being involved in something puts the period inside the other letters

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: end of vile means its final letter
revolutionary means turned round, so the period is read backwards

parts.note: a day is a period of time

explanation.surface: A period of revolution brought vile executions by drowning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end of' reads as 'endless', but NO is taken as written and only the end of vile, E, follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Noyade is the mass drowning used as execution at Nantes during the French Revolution.
